messages:
Jordan: Quick heads-up — starting an access review pass focused on admin/KMS bindings after the last incident. I noticed a few grants without owner tags and one cross-account key policy that lacks proper audit entries. Can security-ops confirm if we have complete CloudTrail/KMS logs back to June?
Sasha: I can take initial triage. Are we talking about customer-facing keys or internal service keys?
Jordan: Internal service keys and a couple onboarding-era project keys. One suspicious grant to proj-legacy that was rotated in May but the KMS logs around rotation time are missing.
Matt: Re: CloudTrail — our central trail was fine but we had a misconfigured S3 bucket lifecycle that archived raw logs early. Putting together a recovery ask to infra.
Leah: If logs are missing we should treat bindings as unverified. Can we freeze privilege escalation paths for the affected roles (admin, infra-admin) while we check evidence?
Jordan: Yes, freeze makes sense for any key with ownerless binding. I want a minimal blast radius — restrict to read-only where possible instead of full remove.
Sasha: Agreed. I'll run the owner-scan and ownerproof flow. Quick snippet: 
```
# scan for ownerless KMS grants
aws kms list-grants --key-id alias/our-service-key | jq '.Grants[] | select(.RetiringPrincipal==null and .GranteePrincipal==null)'
```
Sasha: That will show odd grants, then we run ownerproof link to request evidence.
Matt: ops-bot scheduled a snapshot earlier today; tagging it here: @ops-bot snapshot-1766543000?
ops-bot: snapshot-1766543000 created for project infra-logs. Raw logs stored in s3://redwood-archived-logs/1766543000.tar.gz :white_check_mark:
Leah: Good. Sasha, after you identify ownerless keys, please post a short list in this thread with suggested temporary permission (read-only / deny-exec). Security will authorize.<emoji_clockface>
Sasha: Will do. Also flagging a policy mismatch: some projects used a legacy CloudFormation template that sets KMS key policy with an inline account principal rather than role ARN — harder to track owners. Suggest a CFN lint rule to enforce owner tags.
Jordan: +1 on lint rule. Can we add an automated post-deploy check that alerts on untagged keys?
Matt: Yes — I'll add a CI job that runs `aws resourcegroupstaggingapi get-resources --tag-filters` as part of infra-ci. I'll open a PR to infra/config-ci.
Leah: For immediate remediation, I'm okay with targeted deny-exec for keys with no owner evidence older than 30 days. We should include a rollback plan: revert denies if customer impact observed and create emergency exception ticket.
Sasha: Posting current findings now: key-arn:arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111:key/aaa111 - ownerless, last rotation 2025-05-12; key-arn:arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111:key/bbb222 - owner: infra-jobs (verified).
Sasha: Proposed temp policy for aaa111: set key policy to remove kms:Decrypt for principals other than the backup service role, add annotation `pending-ownerproof: true`.
Jordan: Approve that change. Matt/Leah — please coordinate the change window (low traffic 02:00–04:00 UTC).
Matt: I'll schedule a canary at 02:15 UTC and monitor metrics. If anything trips, roll back in 10m.
Leah: I'll prepare the exception ticket template and notify SRE oncall. Also pinging legal for retention concerns if logs are unrecoverable.
Jordan: One more ask — audit log gap root cause should be included in the postmortem. Quick checklist for the remediation patch: list keys, owner status, temp policy applied, evidence locations, rollback steps, and follow-up lint/CI PRs.
Sasha: Copy. I'll draft the remediation notes and link artifacts here.
ops-bot: deploy-checklist created: remediations/1766543210/ — includes runbook, snapshot link, and ownerproof form :robot_face:
Matt: Thanks. I'll open infra PR and mark it security-sensitive so it gets expedited review.
Jordan: Great work team. We'll reconvene in 24h for status unless something urgent pops. :thumbsup:
